title: CHAPTER 2: APPROACHES TO ETHICS
content:
✨ ሰላም ውድ የ EthioFresh ተማሪዎች!

እንኳን ወደ Chapter 2: Approaches to Ethics በሰላም መጣችሁ! 😉 ይህ ቻፕተር ለMID ፈተናችሁ በጣም አስፈላጊ ከመሆኑም በላይ በዕለት ተዕለት ሕይወታችን የምናደርጋቸውን ውሳኔዎች በምክንያት እንድንመዝን የሚያግዘን ድንቅ ትምህርት ነው።

አይዟችሁ! ኮርሱ ለብዙ ተማሪዎች ሙሉ በሙሉ አዲስና ትንሽ ግራ የሚያጋባ ቢመስልም፣ እኛ ግን ከሞጁሉ አንድም ነጥብ ሳናስቀር፣ የእንግሊዝኛውን ጽሁፍ ሳንቆርጠውና ሳናጥረው፣ ግልጽና ሰፊ የአማርኛ ማብራሪያ አዘጋጅተንላችኋል። በደንብ ከተከተላችሁን ለፈተና ብቁ ከመሆናችሁም በላይ የላቀ እውቀት ይኖራችኋል! 🚀

title: 2.1. Chapter Introduction: The Three Moral Questions (የሞራል ንድፈ-ሐሳቦች መሠረታዊ ጥያቄዎች)
content:
📌 What is Normative/Prescriptive Ethics?
Human beings naturally ask questions about the nature of morality. In the process of prescriptive inquiry, we employ a specific vocabulary. We also invoke theories to explain the nature of morality.

👉 የሰው ልጅ ከተፈጥሮው ጀምሮ ስለ አኗኗሩና ስለ ድርጊቶቹ ትክክለኛነት "ትክክል/ስህተት" እያለ ይጠይቃል። በኤቲክስ ትምህርት ውስጥ ደግሞ እነዚህን ድርጊቶች ለመገምገም የራሳችን የሆኑ ቃላትንና ቲዎሪዎችን እንጠቀማለን።

📌 The 3 Core Questions Every Moral Theory Addresses:
1. What is Good?
👉 ጥሩ ወይም መልካም የሚባለው ነገር በራሱ ምንድን ነው? (ለምሳሌ፡ ደስታ ነው? እውቀት ነው? ወይስ ታማኝነት?)
2. Why is it Good?
👉 ያ ነገር ለምን ጥሩ ተባለ? ጥሩ የሚያደርገው ምስጢሩና ምክንያቱ ምንድን ነው?
3. Where is the Good located?
👉 ይህ መልካምነት የሚገኘው የት ላይ ነው? በድርጊቱ ውጤት ላይ? አድራጊው ባለው አላማ/ግዴታ ላይ? ወይስ በሰውየው በጎ ስብዕና (Character) ውስጥ?

📌 Three Basic Prescriptive Moral Theories:
If there is anything "easy" about moral inquiry, it's the fact that there are only three basic kinds of prescriptive moral theories: Teleological theories, Deontological theories, and Virtue-based theories. Unfortunately, they often provide different and mostly conflicting answers to these basic questions.

👉 ምንም እንኳን ኤቲክስ ሰፊ ቢመስልም፣ የሰዎችን ድርጊት የሚመሩት ዋና ዋና ቲዎሪዎች 3 ብቻ ናቸው፡
1. Teleological (Consequentialist) – በድርጊቱ ውጤት ላይ የሚያተኩሩ።
2. Deontological (Duty-based) – በሕግ፣ በግዴታና በራሱ በድርጊቱ ትክክለኛነት ላይ የሚያተኩሩ።
3. Virtue-based – በሰውየው መልካም ስብዕናና ባህሪ ላይ የሚያተኩሩ።

🎯 Exam Hint: እነዚህ 3ቱ ጥያቄዎች (What, Why, Where) እና 3ቱ መሠረታዊ የሞራል ቲዎሪዎች በፈተና ላይ በ True/False ወይም Matching መምጣታቸው እርግጠኛ ነው! በደንብ ያዟቸው።

title: 2.3. Normative Ethics: Scope and Fundamental Questions (የኖርማቲቭ ኤቲክስ ወሰንና አላማ)
content:
📌 Definition & Purpose of Normative Ethics
We may now begin our review of problems and views in the area of normative ethics, starting with the theory of obligation and then going on to the theory of moral value and nonmoral value. The ultimate concern of the normative theory of obligation is to guide us in making decisions and judgments about actions in particular situations.

👉 ኖርማቲቭ ኤቲክስ ማለት በሕይወታችን ውስጥ አጣብቂኝ ውስጥ ስንገባ "ምን ማድረግ አለብን?" የሚለውን ለመወሰን የሚረዳን መመሪያ ነው።

📌 Humans Play Multiple Roles in Morality:
A main concern is to guide us as agents trying to decide what we should do. But we also want to know what others should do. We are not just Agents in morality; we are also Spectators, Advisers, Instructors, Judges, and Critics.

👉 እኛ በሞራል ዓለም ውስጥ ድርጊት ፈጻሚዎች (Agents) ብቻ አይደለንም። የሌሎችን ድርጊት እንታዘባለን (Spectators)፣ እንመክራለን (Advisers)፣ እናስተምራለን (Instructors)፣ እንፈርዳለን (Judges)፣ እንዲሁም እንወቅሳለን (Critics)!

📌 Core Functions & Approaches of Normative Ethics:
• Offers theories or accounts of the best way to live.
• Evaluates actions systematically by focusing on outcomes, duties, or motivation.
• Includes theories such as utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics, principlism, narrative ethics, and feminist ethics.

📌 Core Questions Posed by Normative Ethics:
1. Are there general principles or rules that we could follow which distinguish between right and wrong?
👉 ትክክልና ስህተትን የሚለዩ አጠቃላይ መመሪያዎች አሉ?
2. Are there virtues and/or relationships that we can nurture, in order to behave well?
👉 መልካም ለመሆን ማሳደግ ያለብን በጎ ስብዕናዎችና ግንኙነቶች አሉ?

title: 2.3.1. Teleological Ethics (Consequentialist) (ውጤት ተኮር የሞራል ንድፈ-ሐሳብ)
content:
📌 Core Concept: "The End Justifies the Means"
What is teleological/Consequentialist ethics? It is referred to as "the end justifies the means". It believes in purpose, ends, or goals of an action. It stresses that the consequences of an action determine the morality or immorality of a given action. An action is judged as right or wrong depending on what happens because of it.

👉 ቴሌኦሎጂ የሚለው ቃል "Teleos" (አላማ/ውጤት) ከሚለው የግሪክ ቃል የመጣ ነው። መመርያው "ግቡ መንገዱን ያጸድቀዋል" ይላል! ምንም ያህል ጥሩ ቅን አላማ ቢኖርህ፣ የድርጊትህ ውጤት መጥፎ ከሆነ ድርጊቱ Morally Wrong ነው ይላል።

📌 Comparative Balance of Good over Evil:
A teleological theory says that the basic criterion of what is morally right is the nonmoral value that is brought into being. An act is right if and only if it produces at least as great a balance of good over evil as any available alternative.

👉 አንድ ድርጊት ትክክል የሚሆነው ከሚመጡት መጥፎ ነገሮች ይልቅ ጥሩ ነገሮች (Balance of Good over Evil) በዝተው ሲገኙ ብቻ ነው ይለናል ።

📌 Moral Value Depends on Non-Moral Value:
For a teleologist, the moral quality of an action depends on the comparative nonmoral value it brings about. To know whether an act is morally right, one must first know what is good in the nonmoral sense.

👉 ድርጊቱ በራሱ ጥሩ ወይም መጥፎ አይባልም። የሚመዝነው የሚያመጣው Non-Moral Good (እንደ ደስታ፣ ስልጣን፣ እውቀት) ነው!

📌 Hedonists vs. Non-Hedonists:
• Hedonists: Identify the good with pleasure and evil with pain (Right action = maximizes pleasure).
• Non-Hedonists: Identify the good with power, knowledge, self-realization, or perfection.

title: Teleological vs. Deontological Ethics: Key Contrast (በሁለቱ ዋና ዋና ቲዎሪዎች መካከል ያለው ልዩነት)
content:
📌 Comparing Deontology and Teleology
Deontological theories deny what teleological theories affirm. They deny that the right, the obligatory, and the morally good are wholly a function of promoting the greatest balance of good over evil.

1. Teleological Theories (Consequentialism):
• Believe there is ONE ultimate right-making characteristic: the comparative value of what is brought into being.
• Focus: Consequences, Future Results.
👉 ድርጊቱ ትክክል የሚሆነው ያመጣው ውጤት አዎንታዊ ሲሆን ብቻ ነው።

2. Deontological Theories (Non-Consequentialism):
• Assert there are other features of the act itself that make it right (e.g., keeping a promise, justice, command of God or State) regardless of consequences.
• Focus: Duty, Rules, Nature of the Act.
👉 ድርጊቱ በራሱ ባለው ባህሪ (ለምሳሌ ቃል ማከበር፣ እውነት መናገር) ይፈረዳል፤ ውጤቱ ምንም ይሁን ምን አያሳስበንም!

🎯 Clarifying Example:
አንድ ሰው ህይወት ለማዳን ሲል ቢዋሽ፡
• Teleologist: መዋሸቱ ትክክል ነው! ምክንያቱም ሰው አድኗል (ውጤቱ ያመረ ነው)።
• Deontologist: መዋሸቱ ስህተት ነው! ምክንያቱም ውሸት በራሱ ተፈጥሮ መጥፎ ነው (ውጤቱ ምንም ይሁን ምን)።

👉 አንዱን ለመምረጥ በጣም አጣብቂኝ ነው። በዚህ ምዕራፍ ውስጥ መልስ ልናገኝለት የሚገባና በአጠቃለይ ምዕራፉን መረዳት የሚያስችለን አንድ ትልቅ ጥያቄ አለ፤ እርሱም አንድን ነገር ምክንያቱን ወይም ውጤቱን መሠረት አድርገን ጥሩ ወይም መጥፎ ብለን Judge የምናደርገውን ድርጊቱን ከማን አንፃር ስናየው ነው? ለዚህ ጥያቄ አንድ መልስ ብቻ የለውም። ለጥያቄኣችን ምላሽ የሚሰጡ በርካታ ፅንሰ-ሀሳቦችን እናያለን፤ ተከታተሉኝ👇👇👇

title: 2.3.2. Egoism: Psychological vs. Ethical Egoism (ራስ ወዳድነት በስነ-ልቦናና በኤቲክስ እይታ)
content:
📌 Scope of Egoistic Consequentialism
Teleologists differ on whose good ought to be promoted. Egoistic CONSEQUENTIALISM only considers how consequences affect oneself or a given group (family, class, or nation).

👉 በቴሌኦሎጂ ውስጥ ውጤቱ የማንን ጥቅም ማስጠበቅ አለበት በሚለው ላይ ልዩነት አለ። ኤጎይዝም "የእኔን/የቡድኔን ጥቅም" ብቻ የሚል ነው። ስለዚህ የድርጊቱ ጥሩነት/መጥፎነት የሚለካው ከራሱ ከድርጊት ፈፃሚው አንፃር ነው ማለት ነው።

📌 Two Core Perspectives on Egoism:

1. Psychological Egoism (Descriptive):
• The viewpoint that humans are not built to look out for other people's interests.
• Claims each of us is always seeking his own greatest good.
• Describes how humans actually behave by nature.
👉 ሰው ልጅ ከተፈጥሮው ጀምሮ የራሱን ጥቅም ብቻ የሚፈልግ ፍጡር ነው (Descriptive - ያለውን እውነታ ይነግረናል)።

2. Ethical Egoism (Normative):
• The view that proper moral conduct consists of "looking out for number one", period.
• Claims that an act is right if and only if it promotes at least as great a balance of good over evil for oneself in the long run.
• Prescribes how humans OUGHT to behave.
👉 ሰው ሁሉ ሁልጊዜ ለራሱ ጥቅም ብቻ መስራት አለበት የሚል መመሪያ ነው (Normative - መሆን ያለበትን ይነግረናል)።

title: 2.3.2.1. Ethical Egoism & The "Twisted Golden Rule" (የኢቲካል ኤጎይዝም መመሪያዎችና አተገባበር)
content:
📌 Case Study: The Good Samaritan
A Good Samaritan stopped to help a stranded motorist on a freeway. The motorist shot and killed the Samaritan, stole his car, and fled.

• Common Moral View: Admire the Samaritan for his altruism and sacrifice.
• Ethical Egoist View: The Samaritan did the WRONG thing! He threw his life away. You have no business stopping for anybody on the freeway.

📌 The Twisted Golden Rule:
• Standard Rule: "Do unto others as you would have them do unto you."
• Egoist Version: "Do unto others SO THAT you will be done unto in a similar way."
👉 ሰዎችን በጥሩ ሁኔታ የምታስተናግዳቸው ለሰዎቹ ብለህ ሳይሆን፣ እነሱም መልሰው በጥሩ ሁኔታ እንዲያስተናግዱህ ለራስህ ስትል ብቻ ነው!

📌 How Ethical Egoists Decide What to Do:
1. List all possible acts.
2. For each act, see how much net good it does for YOU.
3. Identify and choose the act that does the most net good for YOU.

🎯 Important Clarifications on Ethical Egoism:
• Only one's own welfare counts in moral decisions.
• It doesn't forbid helping others, but helping others must stem from how it ultimately helps YOU.
• It doesn't mean doing short-term pleasures (it focuses on long-term benefits like health and safety).

title: 2.3.2.2. Psychological Egoism: Argument & Refutation (ሳይኮሎጂካል ኤጎይዝም እና የፈላስፎች ትችት)
content:
📌 Psychological Argument for Ethical Egoism
Ethical egoism presupposes Psychological Egoism. The argument relies on human nature:
1. We all always seek to maximize our own self-interest.
2. If one cannot do an act, one has no obligation to do that act ("Ought implies Can").
3. Altruistic (selfless) acts involve putting others' interests ahead of our own.
4. Altruism contradicts human nature and is impossible.
5. Therefore, altruistic acts are never morally obligatory.

📌 Philosophical Refutation (Putting the Cart Before the Horse):
Psychological Egoists argue: "Even when you do 'altruistic' things for others, you get satisfaction. That satisfaction was your ultimate goal!"

Critics (Joseph Butler & others) Reply:
• The egoist confuses the object of desire with the satisfaction that results from attaining it.
• You get satisfaction because you wanted to help your friend; you didn't help your friend just to get satisfaction!

👉 ኤጎይስቶች ሰረገላውን ከፈረሱ ፊት አሰልፈዋል! እርካታ ያገኘነው ሌሎችን መርዳት ስለምንፈልግ የመጣ ውጤት እንጂ፣ እርካታ ፍለጋ ብለን አልነበረም የረዳናቸው!

title: 2.3.3. Utilitarianism: The Jigjiga Millionaire Case (ስለ ዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም እና ከሞጅላችሁ ላይ የተወሰደውን የጂጅጋው ባለሀብት ታሪክ አጋራችኋለሁ ተከታተሉኝ👍)
content:
📌 Case Study: The Jigjiga Dying Millionaire Dilemma
You are at Jigjiga with a dying millionaire. He begs you to take $2 Million to Addis Ababa and give it to the Ethiopian Coffee Club (የኢትዮጵያ ቡና ስፖርት ክለብ) to buy better players. You promise him on his deathbed.

When you arrive in Addis Ababa, you see an ad from the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) pleading for $2 Million to save 100,000 starving people and build a sustainable economy.

📌 What is the right thing to do?
• Keep your promise to the dying man and give the money to the Coffee Club?
• Or break your promise and save 100,000 starving people via the Red Cross?

👉 ይህ ትልቅ የስነ-ምግባር አጣብቂኝ ነው! ቃል ማከበር (Deontology) ይሻላል ወይስ የብዙ ሰዎችን ህይወት ማዳን (Utilitarianism)? መልሱን ለናንተ ትተነዋል

title: Traditional Moral Principles vs. Utilitarianism (የተለመዱ መመሪያዎች ለምን አይበቁም?)
content:
📌 Why Traditional Rules Fail in Complex Dilemmas:

1. "Let your conscience be your guide"
• Problem: Subjective. If my conscience says Coffee Club and yours says Red Cross, we reach a dead-end with no room for debate.

2. "Do whatever is most loving"
• Problem: Love is blind. Whom should you love in this situation—the dying millionaire or the 100,000 starving people?

3. The Golden Rule ("Do to others as you would have them do to you")
• Problem: Works in simple situations, but doesn't tell you WHICH party to prioritize when interests conflict.

📌 The Utilitarian Solution:
Unlike Ethical Egoism (which focuses only on the agent), Utilitarianism is a universal teleological system calling for the greatest goodness for the greatest number in society.

"That action is best, which procures the greatest happiness for the greatest numbers."

👉 ዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም ግልጽ መመሪያ ይሰጠናል፡ 2 ሚሊዮን ዶላሩን ለሬድ ክሮስ መስጠት 100,000 ሰዎችን ስለሚያድንና ከፍተኛ ደስታ/ጥቅም ስለሚፈጥር ትክክለኛው ውሳኔ ነው ይላል!

title: 2.3.3.1. Classic Utilitarianism: Bentham & Mill (የዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም መሠረቶች)
content:
📌 Historical Roots & Founders
• Epicurus (342–270 BCE): Ancient Greek philosopher who planted the seeds, stating that pleasure is the goal nature ordained for us. (Mainly focused on individual pleasure).
• Jeremy Bentham (1748–1832) & John Stuart Mill (1806–1873): Formulated Classic Utilitarianism in 18th/19th century Great Britain.

📌 Core Characteristics of Classic Utilitarianism:
1. Secular Social Reformers: Bentham & Mill were optimistic reformists who tried to make law and morality serve actual human needs rather than rigid traditional rules.
2. Universal Teleological System: Maximizes goodness in society as a whole, not just for the individual agent.
3. Hedonistic vs Ideal Utilitarianism:
• Hedonistic Utilitarians (Bentham & Mill): Identify the moral end as the greatest balance of pleasure over pain.
• Ideal Utilitarians (G.E. Moore & Hastings Rashdall): Argue that non-moral goods like beauty, knowledge, and virtue also count, not just pleasure.

title: 🎉 የ Chapter Two Part 1 ትምህርታችን በስኬት አበቃ!
content:
👏 እንኳን ደስላችሁ!

የ Chapter Two (Part 1) ትምህርታችንን በስኬት አጠናቀናል። በዚህ ክፍል የተመለከትናቸው የሞራል ንድፈ-ሐሳቦች (Teleology, Deontology, Ethical & Psychological Egoism, እና Utilitarianism) ለፈተናችሁም ሆነ ለጠቅላላ እውቀታችሁ በጣም ወሳኝ ናቸው።

🎯 Exam Hint / Quick Recap:
• Teleology: ውጤት አቃና/አበላሽ (The end justifies the means).
• Ethical Egoism: ለራስ ጥቅም ብቻ መቆም (Looking out for number one).
• Psychological Egoism: ሰው ከተፈጥሮው ራስ ወዳድ ነው የሚል አመለካከት።
• Utilitarianism: ለብዙሃኑ ህዝብ ታላቅ ደስታና ጥቅም ማምጣት (Greatest happiness for the greatest number).

በቀጣይ የቀሩንን ክፍሎች እንደዚሁ በግልጽና በዝርዝር አዘጋጅተን እናቅርብላችኋለን። በርቱ፣ መልካም የጥናት ጊዜ ይሁንላችሁ! 🎓✨
